title: Which cards are joined by inverses?
description: Two rows of cards are given, and each card in the top row is joined to the card in the bottom row that adds with it to zero. The example pair, minus seven and plus seven, shows the test. Keeko thinks plus five joins plus eight because both have the plus sign, and adding the two cards breaks that doubt.
teaching_notes: One idea: two cards are inverses when their sum is zero, so the match has the same size and the other sign. Watch for students who match cards by the same sign.

source: Connect the inverses by drawing lines. Top row: +5, −7, −8,
video_script.why: A child learns to match numbers with their inverses by testing whether the pair adds to zero.
video_script.substitution: the book's own two rows of cards, joined by the test that the pair adds to zero
video_script.anchor: the two rows of cards from your book in {{NAME_10}}: plus five, minus seven, minus eight, plus nine above; minus nine, plus eight, minus five, plus seven below
video_script.wrong_move: joins cards that look alike, with the same sign, instead of testing whether the sum is zero
video_script.payoff_line: Add the two cards, and a total of zero tells you they are inverses.

final_answer.spoken: plus five with minus five, minus seven with plus seven, minus eight with plus eight, and plus nine with minus nine

names.{{NAME_10}}: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

never_show: any joining line other than the example before the steps
maths_rules: (−7) + (+7) = 0 is the example pair already drawn in the book.
video_script.design: One idea: a pair is inverse when its sum is zero. One picture of two rows throughout; each pair is joined by a line as it is checked. Keeko's doubt is broken by adding plus five and plus eight.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the lift in {{NAME_10}}.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>The top row has plus five, minus seven, minus eight and plus nine.
The bottom row has minus nine, plus eight, minus five and plus seven.
<bookmark mark='example'/>One line is already drawn, from minus seven to plus seven.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which card in the bottom row cancels each card in the top row?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board while the child thinks

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the lift on the ground floor; an up arrow of three floors and a down arrow of three floors end where they began, and the pair is labelled inverses with the sum 0

marks.cancel: the lift rises three floors and drops three floors back to the ground floor
marks.name: the word inverses is written between the two arrows
marks.zero: the sum 0 is written beside the arrows

narration: <bookmark mark='cancel'/>Pressing plus three, and then minus three, brings the lift back to where it began.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Two numbers that cancel each other are called inverses.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>Their sum is zero.

marks.given: the line Given is written on the working board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the top row is plus five, minus seven, minus eight and plus nine.
The bottom row is minus nine, plus eight, minus five and plus seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: the inverse of each top card, joined by a line

marks.find: the line To find is written under Given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to join each top card to its inverse.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the example (−7) + (+7) = 0, so a joined pair adds to 0

marks.example: the drawn line from minus seven to plus seven is highlighted
marks.zero: the sum 0 is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='example'/>Step one, look at the example, minus seven joined to plus seven.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>They add up to zero, so a joined pair must add up to zero.

marks.join: a line is drawn from plus five to minus five
marks.sum: the sum 0 is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step two, join plus five to the card that makes zero with it.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Plus five and minus five make zero.

marks.eight: a line is drawn from minus eight to plus eight
marks.nine: a line is drawn from plus nine to minus nine

narration: <bookmark mark='eight'/>Step three, minus eight joins plus eight, because they make zero.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Plus nine joins minus nine for the same reason.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check that every card is used once and every pair adds to 0

marks.check: each line lights up and the four sums show 0

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check that every card is used once and every pair makes zero.

marks.ans: the answer line is boxed on the working board
marks.ans2: the last two pairs are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Plus five joins minus five, and minus seven joins plus seven.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>Minus eight joins plus eight, and plus nine joins minus nine.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Add the two cards, and a total of zero tells you they are inverses.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two rows of cards
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says +5 joins +8; a line from +5 to +8 is tested and the total +13 appears in the warning colour; the bubble is struck through

marks.sum: plus five and plus eight are added and the total plus thirteen appears

beats.colours: warning colour for the struck bubble and the wrong total
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks plus five joins plus eight, because both have the plus sign.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Add them and see. Plus five and plus eight make plus thirteen, not zero.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>For a pair to cancel, one card has to go the other way.
